discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 261035
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
535 AM EST Thu Nov 26 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Gusty winds and widespread rain develops this afternoon. Winds
  begin to weaken late tonight but rainfall will continue into
  Friday. Winds will gust from 25 to 35 mph later today. A few 
  snowflakes may mix in overnight tonight.
 
- Breezy through Friday with temperatures generally in low to 
  mid 40s.

- Another round of rain is likely Sunday into Sunday evening. 
  Precipitation could end as a mix with wet snow.

- Mainly dry and seasonable Monday through Wednesday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 220 AM EST Thu Nov 26 2026

Trough that dropped south out of central Canada currently
becoming more closed off with tightening pressure gradients and
will push northeast today across the Ohio River valley and into
the northeastern states through Friday. As it does gusty
easterly to northeasterly winds with gusts of 25 to 35 mph 
especially for the eastern third of the CWA will develop later 
this afternoon into tonight. A Gale Warning for southern Lake 
Michigan has been issued for this evening and tonight to address
these gusty winds over the lake. Advected moisture from the 
southeast and Atlantic will also stream northwestward into the 
region today with WAA aloft and isentropic lifting on the 
northeastern quadrant of the low pressure system which will 
bring a steady rainfall across the area later today. Surface
highs though look to remain in the mid 40s. The rainfall will 
spread from the south and push northward across the area into 
this afternoon. A pretty steady plume of moisture aloft and 
subsequent rainfall will continue today and through Friday 
afternoon. Overnight tonight some CAA begins to wrap 
southwestward into the area with the northwesterly portions of 
the system over the area and will allow for some snow showers to
mix in with the rainfall. At this time no real snowfall 
accumulations/impacts are expected. Latest rainfall totals
expected have increased a bit ranging from about 0.75" to 1.25"
with the higher amounts for the southeastern portions of the
area.

As the system pushes northeastward winds will begin to diminish
tonight and the steady rain will look to become more scattered
by Friday afternoon as the storm pulls further away from the
region. A more zonal flow develops over the region and high
temperatures will generally remain in the mid to upper 40s
through Tuesday. Saturday a break in precipitation with a
decrease in clouds as a ridge axis pushes through will allow a
few locations to approach the low 50s. Clouds though look to
increase again by Sunday with another trough albeit weaker than
the first system pushing eastward from the Plains/Midwest 
states across the region which will bring another shot of light
rain to the area. With colder overnight lows by Sunday night
into early Monday morning a few light snow showers as the
precipitation begins to dissipate will be possible. 

Zonal flow continues into next week with mainly dry conditions
and a gradual increase in synoptic heights which will allow 
temperatures to warm with highs by Wednesday and Thursday
getting back into the 50s and a few locales flirting with highs
near 60. By late Wednesday another disturbance arrives with
another chance for some light rainfall.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z FRIDAY/...
Issued at 529 AM EST Thu Nov 26 2026

A few updates to the timing of -RA and degrading ceilings,
especially at KSBN. Latest guidance is favoring a slower
evolution of MVFR ceilings at KSBN as lower ceilings slide ENE 
rather than a northerly route. High confidence in the timing of
rain and MVFR ceilings at KFWA. Similarly high confidence in 
the occurrence of LIFR ceilings as well with a moisture rich 
atmosphere in place. There could be a period of -RASN on either
side of 09z depending on thermal profiles. 

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 4 PM EST this afternoon for LMZ043-
     046.
     Gale Warning from 4 PM this afternoon to 1 AM EST Friday for 
     LMZ043-046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Andersen
AVIATION...Brown

spc.text:
SPC AC 260555

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1155 PM CST Wed Nov 25 2026

   Valid 261200Z - 271200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   EASTERN NORTH CAROLINA...EASTERN VIRGINIA AND SOUTHEAST MARYLAND...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms capable of isolated severe wind gusts and perhaps a
   brief tornado are possible today from parts of eastern North
   Carolina into eastern Virginia and southeast Maryland.

   ...Eastern North Carolina/Eastern Virginia/Southeast Maryland...
   A mid-level shortwave trough will move northeastward today across
   the eastern Carolinas into the Mid-Atlantic. At the surface ahead of
   the approaching trough, a low will deepen inland from the coast. A
   warm front and the associated warm sector to the south will move
   from eastern North Carolina this morning into southeast Virginia
   this afternoon. A band with numerous showers and a few storms will
   be ongoing at the start of the period ahead of the surface low and
   near the warm front. This band will move northward from far eastern
   North Carolina this morning into southeastern Virginia this
   afternoon. RAP forecast soundings at 21Z near and south of the front
   have MUCAPE in the 500 to 1000 J/kg range, with 0-6 km shear around
   65 knots. Hodographs have some curvature in the lowest 1 kilometer.
   This environment could support an isolated tornado threat with
   rotating cells near the warm front within the moist air. The
   stronger cells could also have potential for isolated severe gusts.

   ..Broyles.. 11/26/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 260645

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1245 AM CST Thu Nov 26 2026

   Valid 271200Z - 281200Z

   ...NO THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms are unlikely Friday.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper low will move across the northeastern states on Friday,
   with the primary upper speed max moving farther offshore. At the
   surface, the cold front will already be off the East Coast, with dry
   offshore flow extending southward into the Gulf of America where
   high pressure will reside. Given the stable air mass over land,
   thunderstorms are unlikely across the CONUS.

   ..Jewell.. 11/26/2026

spc.text:
SPC AC 260737

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0137 AM CST Thu Nov 26 2026

   Valid 281200Z - 291200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   A few thunderstorms may develop late Saturday night into parts of
   Arkansas and the Mid South region.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper trough is forecast to develop southeastward into the Plains
   during the day, with the main speed max and midlevel cooling moving
   into MO and AR late. At the surface, the air mass will be stable
   most of the day, until the surface low begins to deepen into MO
   overnight. Southwest winds above the boundary layer will increase to
   over 50 kt from the Sabine Valley into the Mid South, which will aid
   moisture transport atop the surface stable layer.

   Given the antecedent dry conditions, destabilization will be
   minimal. However, steepening midlevel lapse rates and increasing
   large-scale ascent with the approaching strong midlevel wave will
   support increasing precipitation chances from MO into AR and toward
   the MS River by 12Z Sunday.

   Forecast soundings show perhaps 100-300 J/kg MUCAPE, which should
   remain elevated in nature. Therefore, despite strong/favorable wind
   profiles, severe weather is not expected, though scattered
   thunderstorms may develop prior to 12Z Sunday.

   ..Jewell.. 11/26/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
